content.comment_body: I have another question regarding connecting the E3FB-BP22 sensor. I understand the brown wire goes to positive, blue to negative, and if I want to use Light-On PNP mode, I should connect the black wire to the input of the [product_name] controller and possibly bridge it to ground. What type of resistor, if any, is needed for such a connection?

No resistor is required for connecting a PNP sensor to the [product_name] controller input; you can connect the black wire directly to I1...I8. Most sensors with M12 connectors follow the same standard: 1 is brown for supply (DC10-30V), 2 is white for normally closed, 3 is blue for ground, 4 is black for normally open. In your sensor, pin 2 uses pink for switching between light and dark operation modes. Connect this pink wire to either DC24V or ground depending on your application requirements. If your cable is standard, use the white wire where pink is specified. Regards, [user_name]

Hello, You can refer to the sensor manual for wiring details, which I have attached. According to the manual: Brown - 10-30VDC, Black - positive signal to PLC, Blue - 0V, Pink - connect to brown for Light-ON mode, connect to blue for Dark-ON mode.
